title: Athena Tomato (Condor Athena): Characteristics
metaDescription: Athena tomato is an open pollinated tomato variety. See its days to harvest, yield, pest ratings, traits and where it grows best.
excerpt: Athena tomato is an open pollinated tomato variety, also sold or known as Condor Athena or Athena kamatis. It is not a registered variety, so the facts here come from its seller and farm sources. It comes from Allied Botanical (Condor brand).

heroImage.alt: Young tomato plants on silver plastic mulch beds with bamboo stakes in San Ildefonso, Bulacan, the kind of farm where Athena tomato is grown

blocks.text: If you came here looking for Condor Athena or Athena kamatis, this is the same tomato. The facts below come from its seller and from farm sources, each one listed at the end. Compare it with the others in our [tomato variety finder](/crop-varieties/tomato), or see [every crop variety](/crop-varieties) we list. For the crop itself, read our guide: [fertilizer for tomatoes, stage by stage](/blog/fertilizer-for-tomatoes).

blocks.text: How long does it take, and how much does it yield?

Days to harvest, by the seller's count: first harvest 55 to 60 days after transplanting. No trial on record checks this figure yet, so treat it as the seller's own and compare with farms near you before you plan a season around it.

Once you know the day count, anee.io dates every task from each lot's own planting day, with [the growth stages and weather](/features/growth-stages-and-weather) beside it.
Is it resistant to pests and diseases?
No pest or disease ratings are published for this variety. So treat it as untested, and scout every week.

The pests and diseases that hit tomato fields most often: [early blight](/diseases/early-blight), [late blight](/diseases/late-blight), [tomato leaf curl](/diseases/tomato-leaf-curl), [whitefly](/pests/whitefly), [anthracnose](/diseases/anthracnose). Our [pest finder](/pests) and [disease finder](/diseases) help you name what you see.
What its seller and farm sources say

items: **Days to harvest:** First harvest 55 to 60 days after transplanting.
**Fruit:** High round and smooth, green ripening to red, 80 to 100 g, set in several clusters.

blocks.text: These are the seller's own figures, from its own trials. So plant a small area first, and compare it with your usual tomato on the same ground.
Where and when to plant Athena tomato

Bacterial wilt kills more lowland tomato than any other disease, so in the wet season pick a variety rated resistant to it. Choose a firm, oblong fruit if you sell to a far market, and a round, juicy one for fresh sale nearby. Heat tolerant hybrids set fruit in the hot months, when open pollinated tomatoes often drop their flowers. Before planting, get the field ready with our guide: [Land preparation for vegetables](/land-preparation/vegetable-land-preparation).

Ask your municipal agriculturist or nearby farmers how it did in your area last season.

items.q: Is Condor Athena the same as Athena?
items.a: Yes. Condor Athena is another name for Athena. Seed sellers use both, so ask for either one.
Yes. It is open pollinated, so seed from a clean, isolated field grows true. Still, certified seed gives the best start every few seasons.

items.q: Where can I buy seed of Athena?
items.a: Ask an accredited seed dealer in your province, the seller named on this page or your municipal agriculturist. Look for the certified seed tag or a sealed pack before you pay.
